items.rootCause: The audit stores one file-level prefix for the child router.use(durableExports) as empty, rather than composing the parent export router mount from the main application's lazy-loader registration.
items.requiredFix: Compose root-process → parent-router → child-router prefixes, preserving each mount/alias and original registration identity. A file-level first prefix must not substitute for the mount graph.
items.validationCriteria: A real-source parser regression produces /api/export/jobs/:jobId/:action and /api/export/history/:id, never their unprefixed versions. A controlled HTTP/router-stack fixture verifies those exact mounted routes and precedence.
items.productionAcceptanceCriteria: Every affected consumer is rebound to the correct process/path and its actual authorization, durable artifact, failure/retry and cancellation/delete assertions pass from current source.
items.scopeLimit: This proves an inventory defect, not a missing runtime route or a passing export workflow.

items.rootCause: The regex literal branch accepts a backtick TemplateExpression containing interpolation and marks it high-confidence without substituting the finite lexical action binding.
items.requiredFix: Distinguish true string/no-substitution literals from template expressions. Expand only bounded, scope-correct literal bindings; preserve an explicit unknown for all unsupported expressions.
items.validationCriteria: Exactly four current GET/POST × consent/unsubscribe route instances are enumerated under /api/fan-hub, with no literal ${action} path. Shadowed, nonliteral and unbounded bindings stay unresolved.
items.productionAcceptanceCriteria: Each exact alias passes safe GET, CSRF-protected POST, token validation, single-use/expiry and durable preference behavior. Other route aliases cannot supply its acceptance automatically.
items.scopeLimit: This proves an inventory defect, not a successful email delivery or deployed preference journey.
